summary: Provisioning stalls after M.2 Wi-Fi replacement: persistent NIC rename prevents Intune check-in and VPN profile application
description:
Issue summary:
During routine depot repair of several Lenovo units (replacement of M.2 Wi-Fi module), devices enter a provisioning stall on first boot. The provisioning-agent never completes Intune enrollment and the corporate VPN profile fails to push. Devices remain in a limited state: local login works, but corporate policies/patching and VPN are missing, blocking sign-in to internal apps.

Impact:
- Affects small batch of recently repaired machines (3 reported so far) from depot team.
- Blocks end-user access to internal resources until manual remediation.
- Potentially increases repair turnaround time if left undetected.

Environment:
- Depot staging lab (imaging/provisioning flow).
- Windows 11 23H2 build; provisioning-agent v2.4.1; Intune Company Portal version 5.8.0; VPN client: Palo Alto GlobalProtect 6.1.3.
- Hardware: mostly Lenovo M.2 Wi-Fi Module replacements (Intel AX201 → Intel AX211 variants), some devices with vendor firmware mismatch.

Observed behaviour and symptoms:
- During post-repair OOBE/check-in, provisioning logs show repeated failures to apply VPN profile with HTTP 404 from Intune device configuration endpoint.
- local logs indicate NIC persistent naming changed (old NIC GUID persisted in registry, new NIC got a new GUID). Intune seems to look up device network adapter by ID cached earlier in provisioning script.
- If the device is booted without network (airplane mode), the provisioning-agent times out waiting for the expected adapter and aborts enrollment.

Initial theory:
- M.2 Wi-Fi replacement combined with firmware/driver differences is resulting in adapter GUID/instance ID changes. The depot imaging scripts (legacy step) reference the original NIC identity for tagging and early Intune bind operations. When that lookup fails, subsequent steps that push VPN/device policies skip or error.
steps_to_reproduce: Perform M.2 Wi-Fi module replacement on Lenovo device (swap AX201 → AX211)
Boot device into depot imaging OOBE and let provisioning-agent start automated enrollment
Observe provisioning-agent logs / Company Portal output: check for Intune enrollment success/failure
Check registry HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Network\{GUID} for old vs new adapter instance ids
Attempt manual Intune sync from Company Portal and check MDM diagnostic logs
logs:
Excerpt from provisioning-agent.log (2026-03-10 09:12:03):
[ERROR] lookupAdapterById: adapter 'PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_XXXX' not found for expected-id 'NIC-7a3f-2b1c'
[IntuneClient] ApplyDeviceConfiguration 404 Not Found (device-binding failed)
[INFO] provisioning-agent: fallback retry in 30s (attempt 3/3)

System event log: Network Adapter Instance ID changed from '{NIC-7a3f-2b1c}' to '{NIC-94bc-ef01}' after driver install'
investigation_notes: Reproduced locally in depot lab with Lenovo X1 Carbon: replacing AX201 with AX211 reproduced provisioning failure consistently (3/3).
Driver/firmware mismatch observed: AX211 shipped with firmware v1.2.0; depot imaging image includes AX201 drivers which trigger adapter instance rename on driver install.
Provisioning pipeline contains an older helper script that binds VPN profile using hardcoded adapter instance id stored in device metadata during OEM depot tagging step (legacy behaviour).
Intune APIs returning 404 because device object in our device registry was created without the new adapter identifier; agent tries to POST to device-specific endpoint constructed using old id.
No indications of upstream Intune outage — isolated to devices with adapter GUID change.
temporary_workarounds: Manual remediation: Windows admin can force Intune re-enrollment (Settings → Access work or school → Disconnect → Enroll) and run Company Portal sync. This restores policies and VPN profile.
Apply a short-lived PowerShell helper on depot: regenerate NIC mapping by running 'Get-NetAdapter | New-GuidRemapScript' and re-run provisioning-agent hooks.
If VPN is still missing, reinstall GlobalProtect after Intune policy sync (order matters).
root_cause: Legacy depot tagging and provisioning helper scripts rely on a NIC instance identifier recorded at time of OEM tagging. Post-repair M.2 Wi-Fi swaps change the adapter instance id and the provisioning flow lacks a resilient lookup, causing Intune binding to fail.
resolution:
Implemented a short-term depot-side fix: updated the imaging pre-provision script to detect adapter instance changes and use a network-agnostic lookup path (match by MAC OUI + driver signature) to bind the device record. Deployed new helper (provision-fix-v1) to depot-staging on 2026-03-12.

Operational remediation steps performed:
- Deployed updated script to depot staging images.
- Reprocessed the three affected devices with updated script — all three successfully completed Intune enrollment and received VPN profile.
- Created a follow-up task to upstream the change into baseline image and add unit tests to depot CI.
follow_up_actions: Patch baseline imaging image with provision-fix-v1 and include AX211 drivers to avoid instance renames post-driver install (Owner: Depot Eng, due 2026-03-19)
Add a post-repair verification step in depot runbook to run Intune sanity check (check Company Portal MDM status and VPN profile), update repo runbook (Owner: SRE-Endpoint)
Audit depot spare-part firmware versions and create gating rule to refuse module swaps if firmware mismatch detected (Owner: HW Ops)
Add telemetry for adapter-instance-change events to provisioning logs so detection is automated (Owner: Provisioning Team)
Create KB for field repair techs describing manual remediation steps and link to to Confluence page
